title: Introducing Basedash as code
summary: The Basedash public API now covers chart settings, dashboard verification and AI context, so you can manage Basedash from your own code.
body_markdown:
Today we’re launching **Basedash as code** . The Basedash public API now covers the configuration behind your charts and dashboards: every chart setting, dashboard verification, and the AI context on your tables and columns.


Configuring a BI tool usually means clicking through settings panels, one chart at a time, and hoping nobody changes them later. Now you can create, read, and update that configuration from your own code, and keep Basedash in sync with it.


Every endpoint lives under` https://charts.basedash.com/api/public/organizations/{orgId}` and takes a Bearer API key that belongs to a workspace admin.


## Every chart setting, from the API


` POST /charts` and` PATCH /charts/{id}` now accept the fields from the chart settings panel:


- **Number format:** number, currency, or percentage, plus the currency code and full numbers
- **Labels and legend:** the metric label and the legend
- **Goal line and axes:** a goal line and the axis minimum and maximum
- **Bars and colors:** stacked or grouped bars, and series and segment colors
- **Everything else:** image and text properties, the map variant, and table column widths and pins


```text
BASE  =  "https://charts.basedash.com/api/public/organizations/  $ORG_ID  "


curl   -X   PATCH   "  $BASE  /charts/  $CHART_ID  "   \
-H   "Authorization: Bearer   $BASEDASH_API_KEY  "   \
-H   "Content-Type: application/json"   \
-d   '{
"numericalFormat": "CURRENCY",
"currencyCode": "USD",
"goalLineValue": 150000,
"seriesColor": "PURPLE"
}'
```


` GET /charts/{id}` and` GET /dashboards/{dashboardId}/charts` return the same fields, so you can read a chart’s full configuration, copy it to another chart, or keep it in sync. Every new field is optional, so your existing requests behave exactly as before.


## Verify dashboards with one request


[Verified dashboards](https://www.basedash.com/blog/introducing-verified-dashboards) tell your team which numbers to trust. You can now verify one from code: send` verified: true` to` PATCH /dashboards/{id}` , or` verified: false` to remove the verification.


```text
{   "verified"  :   true   }
```


Dashboard responses include` verifiedAt` and` verifiedByMemberId` , so you can see when a dashboard was verified and by whom. The same admin rule and audit log events apply as when you verify in the app.


## AI context for every column


The AI context on your tables and columns is what helps Basedash understand your data.` GET /data-sources/{id}/catalog` lists a data source’s schemas, tables, and columns with their Basedash description (the AI context), the database’s own comment (read-only), their display name, and their visibility.


` PATCH /data-sources/{id}/catalog` updates descriptions, display names, and visibility in batches:


```text
{
"changes"  : [
{
"schemaName"  :   "public"  ,
"tableName"  :   "orders"  ,
"columnName"  :   "amount"  ,
"description"  :   "Order total in USD, after refunds"  ,
"expectedDescription"  :   "Order total in USD"
}
]
}
```


- **Up to 1000 changes per request.** A batch applies all or nothing, so if any change fails, none of them do.
- **No silent overwrites.** Add an optional` expectedDescription` , and the write is rejected with a 409 if someone changed the text since you read it.


## Getting started


Basedash as code is available today through the public API.


1. [Sign up for Basedash](https://charts.basedash.com/signup) or log in as a workspace admin
2. Create an API key in **Settings → API keys**
3. Send your first request to` https://charts.basedash.com/api/public/organizations/{orgId}`


Authentication, endpoints, and request formats are covered in the[API reference](https://www.basedash.com/docs/api-reference/overview) . For everything else the API can do, see the[Basedash developer platform](https://www.basedash.com/blog/introducing-the-basedash-developer-platform) launch.


**Basedash, as code.**
